segments.title: Chương 27: 0027 [Nương Nương]
segments.content:
The boss was installing and adjusting the satellite dish.

This kind of satellite dish could even receive foreign television channels.

Strictly speaking, it was illegal, but no one would bother a farmer over it.

Because the cost of enforcement was too high.

Amidst the joyful laughter, another farmer's wife came running, out of breath. "My old man is working in Zhejiang, he took the IOU with him..."

"Took it with him" was probably an excuse; this family had most likely lost the IOU.

Chen Guiliang didn't waste words, pulling out the ink pad he had swiped from the game studio. "It's alright. Aunty Liu, you can just write a receipt. The elders here are all witnesses. I'll pay back your family's debt, principal and interest all included."

A villager immediately started flattering, "Guiliang is as upright as his dad. So straightforward, he's definitely going to be very successful!"

As long as you succeed, you will be surrounded by good people.

You will feel that this world is a wonderful place.

"You're too kind, too kind."

Chen Guiliang opened three packs of Hongtashan cigarettes in a row, passing them around to the men who had successively gathered to watch the excitement.

Grandma also took out the sponge cake her grandson had bought, handing it out to any woman or child she saw.

With cigarettes and cake clearing the way, praises were heard without end.

Chen Guiliang watched with a faint smile, observing silently. It was as if he were watching a real-life comedy.

"Young man, the satellite dish is all adjusted. You can get dozens of channels now." The boss emerged from the house.

Chen Guiliang opportunely handed the boss a cigarette, then said to his grandpa and the others, "Grandpa, Grandma, Youngest Uncle, I'll be going now. There's still another color TV by the roadside."

"I'll see you off," said Grandpa.

Chen Guiliang said, "No need, I'll take the three-wheeler. The color TV's been bought, you all should go watch it."

Grandpa, Grandma, and Youngest Uncle, surrounded by the onlooking villagers, saw Chen Guiliang all the way to the side of the village road, watching him climb into the back of the three-wheeler.

In the southwestern region, villages were sparsely populated, with a few households here and a few there, unlike the more concentrated settlements on the plains.

Although Chen Guiliang's parents were from the same village, their homes were quite far apart.

He sat in the three-wheeler, continuing to jolt along for a while, and finally returned to his own home.

The same scene played out once more.

Chen Guiliang didn't even need to go door-to-door to repay debts; the creditors came running as soon as they heard the news. Even creditors from the neighboring village rushed over on motorcycles or bicycles.

A neighbor even took the initiative to inform Grandma, who was up in the mountains cutting firewood. She hurried home, carrying a large bundle of wood on her back.

"Grandma, my dad struck it rich. He'll be able to come back for the New Year," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

Grandma appeared unusually calm. "It's good that the debts are cleared."

She had been a young lady from a landlord's family, having not only attended a private traditional school but also a modern one.

She was a widow who had remarried, at the time bringing along her son who had just turned one—Chen Guiliang's father.

In other words, Chen Guiliang's father was only Grandpa's stepson.

Ignoring the compliments from the neighbors, Grandma went about her business, stacking the firewood as if everything happening around her had nothing to do with her.

Grandpa, Second Uncle, and Second Aunt also hurried over.

Second Aunt was particularly enthusiastic, helping Grandma with the housework for the first time ever.

Chen Guiliang just smiled and said nothing.

"Guiliang, I heard your dad struck it rich?" Second Uncle, Chen Xingmin, was genuinely happy.

Chen Guiliang took out a pack of Hongtashan and tossed the whole thing to Second Uncle with a smile.

Chen Xingmin caught it with an outstretched hand, stuffed it into his pants pocket and said, "Good smokes."

The uncle and nephew stood there chatting, occasionally dealing with the villagers and creditors.

Chen Guiliang was only willing to chat with his second uncle, but couldn't be bothered to even glance at his grandfather or second aunt.

Before his rebirth, Chen Guiliang had even feigned being busy to avoid attending his grandfather's funeral.

Stepson, step-grandson—in some people's eyes, they weren't real children and grandchildren.

Their relationship was worse than that with an outsider.

There was no affection, only resentment; the differential treatment had been too severe.

Of course, the relationships among the younger generation were quite good. Chen Guiliang got along well with his cousins.

His father, second uncle, and aunt—the three siblings were also extremely close. Because his second uncle and aunt were raised by his father, he was truly a fatherly older brother.

"Guiliang, I heard your dad made hundreds of thousands?" Second Aunt, holding some firewood, deliberately circled around to ask.

Chen Guiliang said, "Yeah."

Second Aunt immediately said, "Guirong's (male cousin) grades aren't good, and he has the high school entrance exams next year. I'm planning to send him to No. 1 High School, and we might have to pay an out-of-district fee. Could we borrow ten thousand yuan from your dad?"

Chen Guiliang looked at Chen Xingmin. "Second Uncle, do you want to borrow money? As long as you ask, I'll go figure something out."

"No," Chen Xingmin shook his head repeatedly. "Whichever school Guirong can get into is the one he'll attend. There's no need to pay an out-of-district fee to get into a better school."

Second Aunt immediately shot a vicious glare at her husband. The couple would probably get into a fight tonight, with Second Uncle usually being the one who took the beating.

A henpecked husband, a tigress.

"Guiliang, I'm heading out," Chen Xingmin didn't want to watch his wife make a fool of herself here any longer.

Chen Guiliang waved his hand. "Take care, Second Uncle."

Seeing that she couldn't borrow the money, Second Aunt instantly dropped the act. She threw down the firewood in her hands and left, not even willing to carry it a few meters away to stack it properly.

Grandpa stood at the door, having been looking for a chance to speak the whole time.

But Chen Guiliang didn't even look him in the eye.

Grandpa stood there for a while, then had no choice but to turn and leave, taking a hoe from under the eaves on his way out.

Chen Guiliang reminded him, "That's my family's."

"I'm just borrowing it," Grandpa said as he walked away with the hoe on his shoulder.

Chen Guiliang said sarcastically, "Remember to bring it back. The things my parents left at home, even the creditors didn't want them, but they've nearly all been carried off by you over the years."

When Chen Guiliang's father and second uncle divided the family property, Grandpa and Grandma also split up to live with the two sons.

Even after the split, Chen Guiliang's family still had to give Grandpa grain every year. If they didn't, Grandpa would make a scene, going to the village chief to complain that his eldest son was unfilial.

Having been reborn, Chen Guiliang no longer hated anyone, but no one should expect him to like them either.

He would never forget the Spring Festival of his third grade year. He was playing with his cousins, and they went to the teahouse to ask their grandpa, who was playing cards, for money to buy snacks.

His cousins each got 50 cents. He lingered, wanting some too.

In front of everyone in the teahouse playing cards, Grandpa gave him a harsh slap and yelled, "Get lost, don't squander my money!"

As the sky gradually darkened, the crowd of onlookers left one by one.

The boss who sold the color TV had also driven off in his three-wheeler long ago.

Only Chen Guiliang and his grandmother were left at home.

From the time Chen Guiliang got home until now, Grandma had only said one sentence. Now, she silently went to cook.

Chen Guiliang followed her into the kitchen, wanting to say something but not knowing how to begin.

He glanced at the water vat, then turned to grab the buckets to fetch water from the well a hundred-odd meters away.

Bucket after bucket, until the water vat was full.

"Dinner's ready." Grandma finally spoke.

Chen Guiliang quickly went to bring out the food. The grandmother and grandson sat around the table in the main room, the newly bought color TV playing a drama.

Two dishes and a soup. The meat dish was fried pork fat cracklings.

Grandma was very frugal. Only when Chen Guiliang came home would she cook a meat dish.

The so-called meat dish was either pork cracklings or meat from the pig's jowl.

Moreover, this was a luxury he only got after starting high school. In junior high, it was vegetables every meal; he could only see meat during festivals.

That was why when Chen Guiliang was in junior high, he once had a grand dream: to eat meat once a month!

Chen Guiliang walked over to the TV. "Grandma, this is the power switch."

Grandma said, "I know, I've used a TV before."

When Chen Guiliang was in elementary school, his family had a black-and-white TV, which was later carried away by an angry creditor.

"This one's different. You can use the remote to turn it on and off."

Chen Guiliang brought the remote over. "This button is the power switch. This one changes the channel, this one adjusts the volume..."

Grandma listened intently.

She had a very good memory. Back when the villages ate from a communal kitchen, Grandma had worked as a point-keeper for the production team.

Being a point-keeper was a very sought-after job, as one could get more work points for team members and their families. But Grandma never played favorites, doing things by the book, which made both the team members and her family complain about her.

"That dish on the roof is called a satellite dish. It can pick up satellite channels," Chen Guiliang said. "The TV seller has already adjusted it, so it's best not to mess with it. If a strong wind blows the dish out of alignment and you can't get some channels, just wait for me to come back on break to fix it."

Grandma said, "You can teach me."

Chen Guiliang stopped eating and taught his grandmother, step-by-step, how to adjust the satellite dish.

In less than ten minutes, Grandma had completely mastered it.

She adjusted it back and forth herself, then started changing channels, stopping after a while.

This channel was broadcasting Sichuan opera.

Grandma stared at the TV while eating slowly.

The way she ate was particularly elegant, chewing slowly in small bites, as if she were still that young lady from a landlord's family decades ago.

"The lyrics have been changed?" Grandma muttered to herself.

Chen Guiliang said, "The Sichuan opera on TV has probably been revised. It's different from what you used to listen to. The lyrics and spoken parts have been changed to be more in line with the times. Some of the cruder content has also been deleted or revised."

Grandma commented, "The changes aren't good."

Chen Guiliang tried to cheer her up. "When I have money in the future, I'll support an opera troupe and have Grandma be in charge of reviewing the lyrics."

"Then I'll be waiting," Grandma revealed a smile.

In Chen Guiliang's eyes, his grandmother's smile was more beautiful than the moon over the borderlands. He had rarely seen her smile throughout his entire childhood.

Grandmother and grandson sat in the main room chatting. Grandma watched TV until very late.

In the middle of the night, as Chen Guiliang was drifting in and out of sleep, he seemed to hear someone singing opera in a low voice.

"Red apricot blossoms fill the courtyard with fragrance, loneliness unknowingly gives way to the bloom of youth. Ever since my darling Zheng went to the capital, I miss him nine times a day..."

Looks like Grandma will have a good impression of the opera-singing girl Bian Guanyue in the future. Little Bian's position as the main wife is a little more secure.
